title: The Old Tiger and the Gold Bracelet
text:
An old tiger lived beside a lake. He had become too weak to hunt, so he sat on the bank after bathing, holding a gold bracelet in his paw, and called out to passing travelers that he would give it away as an act of charity.

A traveler heard him and was tempted, but he was not a fool. It was a fine bracelet, but its owner was a tiger. He asked how he could trust a creature that killed people.

The tiger had an answer ready. In his youth, he admitted, he had done many wicked things and killed many men and cattle. But he had lost his wife and children, and a holy man had taught him to give alms and live righteously. Now he was old, his claws were worn and his teeth had fallen out. Who could fear him? He only wished to give the bracelet to a worthy man. But first the traveler must bathe in the lake, as was proper before receiving a gift.

The traveler, convinced, waded into the lake. He sank deep into the mud and could not get out. The tiger said he would come and help him, walked over, and seized him. As he was being killed, the traveler reflected that he had trusted a tiger.
lesson: Tempting offers from people with a known record of harm deserve the most skepticism, especially when the offer comes with a story of reform and conditions that put you in their reach.
